heard: A distant star seems to shine with short-lived radioactive elements. We expect stars to be made of hydrogen, with atmospheres containing common metals like iron. In 1961, astronomer Antoni Przybilski analyzed a star 356 light years away. Its spectrum showed almost no iron, but was swamped by rare earth elements thousands of times more abundant than in our sun. Weirder still, early reports identified promethium, a radioactive element with a half-life of only 17.7 years. In a billion-year-old star, these elements should have decayed away eons ago. While physicists hypothesized exotic nuclear decay, 2023 analyses contested the finding due to severe spectral line crowding. Yet, the longest lived of these elements decay away in just 17.7 years.
